updates.rationale: The accepted pruning theorem makes multiletter Marton achievability a concrete active program, but it neither supplies an improving law nor resolves three- and four-symbol supports. Program-level work remains for coordinating structural reductions, certified optimization, and comparison with the converse target.

The submission identifies a precise follow-up agenda—an improving two-letter witness must use at least three super-input symbols—but prioritizing support classes, numerical searches, and certification strategies still requires modest planning work.

Access eliminates the singleton and all six two-symbol support cases through symmetry classification, cooperative outer bounds, and a certified repetition-orbit estimate. Substantial work remains to obtain analogous reductions or decisive bounds for the structurally harder three- and four-symbol supports.

The theorem sharply removes low-support candidates but leaves a nonconvex search over three- and four-symbol super-input laws, auxiliary variables, and certified rate evaluations. A sizable computational and analytic search remains plausible if structural pruning does not settle those cases.
